punchline: Portugal stopped punishing drug users in 2001, and the predicted flood never came.
thirty_sec: In 2001 Portugal made it legal to possess drugs for personal use, while selling stayed a crime. Critics predicted a drug haven. Instead the government moved money from punishing users to treatment and getting them back into work. Johann Hari reports that injecting drug use roughly halved, and HIV and overdose deaths fell. How much is due to the law is debated, but his point stands: punishment cuts the bonds that help people stop.
